request.system: You are a senior clinical coder in an Australian public hospital with fifteen years of experience coding inpatient episodes in ICD-10-AM. You are careful, conservative, and you never invent a code you are not sure of the chapter for.

messages.content:
Code the episode of care below. The principal diagnosis is the single condition established after investigation to be chiefly responsible for the patient's episode of admitted care. It is not the patient's most serious comorbidity, not the presenting symptom, and not the procedure performed. Give the three-character ICD-10-AM category for the principal diagnosis.

Hospital course:
Discharge Summary

Patient Name: [redacted]
Medical Record Number: [redacted]
Date of Admission: April 30, 2020
Date of Discharge: May 21, 2020

Hospital Course:
The patient was admitted to the GHESKIO MDR-TB hospital on April 30, 2020, with persistent fever, cough, and weight loss. He was diagnosed with COVID-19 and transferred to a separate building to prevent the spread of the virus. The patient did not require oxygen therapy and recovered from COVID-19 three weeks following diagnosis. He was continued on antituberculous therapy without complication.

Medical History:
The patient presented with a history of chronic cough, fever, and weight loss. He was evaluated by the medical staff with a physical examination, chest radiograph, and sputum analysis. The chest radiograph demonstrated a large right upper lobe cavity, with right middle lobe opacity and right hilar fullness. The GeneXpert sputum test was positive for the presence of Mycobacterium tuberculosis with probable resistance to rifampin. The patient was lost to follow-up before hospitalization and initiation of therapy.
Discharge Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Follow-Up:
The patient is advised to continue regular follow-up with his healthcare provider. He is instructed to complete the prescribed antituberculous therapy and to maximize precautions against COVID-19 to prevent further spread.

Discharge Condition:
The patient was discharged in stable condition. He was advised to follow-up with his healthcare provider and to continue antituberculous therapy as prescribed.

Discharge Medications:
Antituberculous regimen composed of bedaquiline, levofloxacin, linezolid, clofazimine, and pyrazinimide was initiated and continued throughout hospitalization.

Discharge Instructions:
The patient is advised to follow-up with his healthcare provider. He should continue the prescribed antituberculous therapy and maximize precautions against COVID-19 to prevent further spread.

Answer in the form CODE: <letter><digit><digit>

text:
The patient was admitted to an MDR-TB hospital with fever, cough and weight loss. Workup showed pulmonary TB with probable rifampin resistance (GeneXpert positive, cavitary disease). COVID-19 was diagnosed after admission and did not need oxygen. The antituberculous regimen was started on admission and continued throughout the stay.

The principal diagnosis is the condition established after study to be chiefly responsible for the admission. That is pulmonary tuberculosis, not COVID-19. COVID-19 was diagnosed during the stay, so it is an additional diagnosis. Under ICD-10-AM, U07.1 would be used for the COVID-19.

Tuberculosis of the lung sits in A15–A19. Bacteriologically confirmed pulmonary TB is A15.x. Rifampin resistance is an additional code, U82.x, for resistance to beta-lactam antibiotics and other antimicrobials (U82–U84), so it does not change the category of the principal diagnosis.

CODE: A15
